newsitem.title: USA: Teamsters' Carey to hold news conference.
newsitem.headline: Teamsters' Carey to hold news conference.

text.p: The president of the Teamsters union, Ron Carey, will hold a "major news conference" to discuss developments in the 15-day-old strike against United Parcel Service, the Teamsters said on Monday.
The Teamsters gave no other details on the content of the pending news conference, which was to take place at Teamsters' headquarters here at 10:15 p.m. EDT (0215 GMT Tuesday).
Moments after announcing Carey's planned news conference, the Teamsters said it would be delayed for 30 minutes, to begin at 10:45 p.m. (0245 GMT).

Earlier in the day, UPS Chairman James Kelly said the company and the union had made progress toward settling the strike but predicted it could go "much, much longer" if negotiations were to break off this week.
The strike by 185,000 Teamsters has crippled the nation's largest carrier of small packages, costing UPS $650 million in lost business so far.

The two sides had resumed talks Thursday at the request of Labor Secretary Alexis Herman. The talks continued with only brief breaks for sleep until late Sunday night, when they adjourned for 12 hours, before resuming again on Monday.
